## Highlights

- Signing in with a password on a browser where someone else is still signed in works again: the sign-in starts a session of your own, and the other person's session is left for them to end. Before, it was refused and the sign-in page said the password was wrong, the known limitation the v0.5.88 notes described ([#4919](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4919)).
- A member whose single sign-on session belongs to one organization and who opens a link into another is told that the session is limited to the organization that signed them in, with **Sign in to this workspace**, instead of being told they are not a member. Single sign-on members have **Log out** and **Sign in again** back. A session an authenticating proxy asserted gets no such button ([#4908](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4908)).
- A refused or stalled organization switch no longer looks done: it says "Couldn't switch to" the organization, with **Try again** and **Back** to the organization you are still in, after at most 20 seconds ([#4887](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4887)). When `/dashboard` cannot read your organizations or open one, it says so with **Try again** and **Sign in again** instead of a frame that never moves on ([#4825](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4825)). A **Settings › Account** tab that was open while another tab turned [two-factor authentication](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/two-factor-authentication) on or off now says so and shows the current state, instead of an English error ([#4768](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4768)).
- When a read fails (a lost connection, a server fault or an ended session), Tale says so and offers **Try again** where it showed an empty, missing or denied state before. A task opened as a page reads "Couldn't load this task." instead of **Page not found** ([#4587](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4587)). A [shared chat](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/shared-threads) link reads "Couldn't load this shared chat." instead of saying its owner withdrew it ([#4535](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4535)). The ⌘K search names a failed search instead of answering **No results**, and keeps the results that did load when only part of it failed ([#4890](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4890)). **What's new** no longer spins for good or says "You're up to date." over no notes ([#4900](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4900)). A file's version history ([#4577](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4577)), a project's metrics ([#4588](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4588)), a project that failed to load rather than one that was deleted ([#4605](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4605)), website search ([#3860](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/3860)), the bell's notifications ([#4665](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4665)), the writes that wait for approval ([#4766](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4766)), and an automation's model list ([#4765](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4765)), versions and tests ([#4828](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4828)) do the same, and so does a project agent's **Skills, connectors & tools** menu, which read as "No skills in this organization yet." with every equipped skill unavailable ([#4697](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4697)). **New project** no longer drops **Who can see it** while its team list loads or after that read failed, which created the project for the whole organization ([#4836](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4836)), and a failed refresh of your membership no longer empties Knowledge or leaves Governance, Metrics and most Settings pages loading ([#4859](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4859)).
- Settings name a failed read the same way instead of showing an empty list, a wrong default or **Access denied**: API access ([#4767](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4767)); Teams, Notifications and Enterprise SSO ([#4653](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4653)); WebDAV app-passwords ([#4652](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4652)); the Skills library ([#4888](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4888)); Usage, Sandboxes and **API › Models** ([#4832](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4832)); audit log, erasure and guardrail views ([#4834](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4834)); the API key owner pickers ([#4586](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4586)); a project's default reviewer ([#4644](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4644)); and the organization's default for custom instructions, which showed an unchecked switch while chat kept applying them ([#4889](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4889)). Legal hold and Trash name why a request was refused in the reader's language, and the competence member picker no longer says "No members found" while it loads ([#4840](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4840)). A form no longer flags your next draft as changed in another session after you discard or save, as the standard agent editor in Governance did after its own switch saved ([#4049](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4049)).
- [Files in chat replies](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/files-and-skills#open-and-download-the-files): an SVG a reply made shows as a file card with **Open** and **Download**, where nothing showed before ([#5028](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5028)), and a reply that says it attached a file its turn never stored now carries "No file was attached to this reply." ([#5168](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5168)). With [image generation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/content-models#let-agents-generate-images) off, chat says that pictures cannot be made and that an Admin or Owner turns it on under **Settings › Governance › Models › Image generation**, instead of drawing an SVG in place of a photo ([#5029](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5029)).
- [Uploading a skill bundle](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/workspace/skills#import-an-existing-bundle) asks whom the skill is for, with the **Visibility** field a new blank skill has, and stores that choice in place of what the bundle declares; `POST /api/app/skills/upload` takes an optional `visibility` (`team` or `org`) and `teams` ([#5032](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5032)).
- [Dictation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/voice-mode#dictate-and-check-a-message): sending while you dictate waits, up to 30 seconds, for the last words before the message leaves. Before, they landed in the emptied field after it was sent. A running dictation can be sent without stopping it first ([#5034](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5034)). The chat composer stays compact on laptop screens instead of taking a third of them ([#5035](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5035)).
- The chat assistant's web fetch follows a redirect onto another host, over HTTPS only and with every hop checked as before, so a page such as Firefox's release notes on `www.mozilla.org`, which redirect to `www.firefox.com`, is read instead of refused. A bot-check page is never handed to the model as the page's text; through [outbound proxies](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/environment-reference#outbound-proxies) it is asked for again through the next proxy, up to three attempts within 15 seconds. A message with a transcribed video link is no longer refused with "attachments.0.fileSize: Invalid input".
- Through a model gateway such as Bifrost, OpenAI tool models keep their tool calls whole: two calls that arrive under the same index are no longer run together into one invalid call, and direct chat asks the gateway's Responses API for models whose tools OpenAI serves only there, so a call's arguments are no longer lost. A gateway that refuses the Responses API is asked on Chat Completions as before. Usage is now booked for a streamed reply that a refusal cut off inside a tool call ([#4050](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4050)). Replacing an OpenAI subscription key no longer asks for the ChatGPT account ID again: left empty, the stored ID is kept ([#4830](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4830)).
- A task's board card and list row say why its run waits, in the words of its Run row, instead of looking idle ([#5147](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5147)). A run whose sandbox host refused to start it moves to another worker of its agent that can start, such as one on a connected sandbox device with room, instead of asking the full server again until it gives up after 12 hours ([#5006](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5006)). A comment that restarts a run's turn while its sandbox has no room waits for room instead of failing the run ([#4720](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4720)). A project agent's question opens the run that waits for your answer instead of the task board ([#3632](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/3632)), and an answer whose delivery the sandbox refused for lack of memory resumes the conversation that asked instead of starting the step over ([#4719](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4719)). See [waiting and failed runs](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/task-automation#handle-waiting-and-failed-runs).
- A run that keeps running out of memory is retried three times, 2, 10 and 30 minutes apart, then fails for good with the out-of-memory notice. Before, an attempt that worked 15 minutes reset its retry budget, so it was retried without end and paid for the model each time. The per-task hourly limit on retries now counts every automatic retry, those of a run a person started included; a person's own start is never counted ([#5148](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5148)). A failure with no retry left is announced at once instead of up to 30 minutes later ([#4717](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4717)). An automation's agent step whose model was at capacity keeps that account for its retry a minute later, instead of the retry skipping a healthy account ([#4530](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4530)).
- Tasks and boards: a member removed from the organization reads **Former member** in task views instead of a raw user ID ([#3788](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/3788)); a refused drag puts the card back in its column ([#4838](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4838)); the **+N** label chip can be focused to show the hidden labels, and a filter that matches nothing says "No tasks match these filters." with **Clear filters** ([#4910](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4910)); search boxes and filters over an empty list are disabled, as a table's already were ([#2802](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/2802)); and switching between Knowledge tabs, Settings pages or projects no longer fades the page in again.
- Projects and organizations: a suggested project key keeps accented letters ("Société Générale" gives `SG`, "Łódź Port" gives `LP`), and existing keys are unchanged ([#4782](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4782)). The organization wizard accepts names such as "Müller AG", "Société Générale" and "Smith & Co." ([#4886](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4886)). **New folder** in a project's files says why a name is refused: a slash, a control character, or only dots ([#4837](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4837)). Renaming a project no longer says "Project created", and refused uploads keep their reasons instead of hiding them behind "+N more file(s) were skipped" ([#4892](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4892)).
- Knowledge and records: an open **Edit** of a knowledge entry keeps its draft when another member saves the entry, and shows that a newer version exists ([#4860](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4860)). The Products list offers a **Category** filter ([#3866](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/3866)). Only people who may delete websites get the Websites list's checkboxes and **Delete selected**; a Contacts or Products import with a missing column says which, in the reader's language; and saving a contact with another contact's email names the duplicate ([#4841](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4841)). A document's indexing **Retry** is no longer overwritten as failed by a sweep of stuck documents that ran at the same moment ([#4158](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4158)). In the Microsoft 365 file picker, clearing the header checkbox over search results no longer clears the files picked through earlier searches ([#3921](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/3921)).
- Notifications: a row opened from the expanded **Notifications** dialog closes the dialog ([#3903](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/3903)); a notification that a newer event rewrote moves to the bell's first page ([#3630](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/3630)); and a comment on a task with many watchers notifies them in a fixed number of database round trips, 13 instead of 278 for 25 watchers and 25 mentions ([#4712](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4712)). [Notifications and the bell](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/member/preferences#notifications) have a guide now ([#4509](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4509)), and so do [the organization's settings and its deletion](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/organization) ([#4508](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4508)).
- [Personal data masking](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/guardrails#protect-personal-data) masks an email address whose local part is written in any alphabet, whole ([#4777](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4777)); a date of birth with a two-digit year after a keyword, such as "DOB: 15/03/87", "Geburtsdatum: 15.03.87" or "date de naissance : 15/03/87" ([#4776](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4776)); and an IPv6 address that ends in `::`, such as `2001:db8:abcd:12::` ([#4778](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4778)). Each went through unmasked before.
- [Single sign-on](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/enterprise-sso#assign-roles-and-teams-at-sign-in) reads a claim whose name contains dots as written: an Auth0 namespaced claim (`https://example.com/roles`), the Microsoft role claim URI or a `urn:oid` SAML attribute. Claim rules and the name, email and groups mappings that named one never matched, and the member signed in with the default role ([#4775](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4775)). [SCIM](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/enterprise-sso#provision-members-through-scim) stores the `externalId` a PATCH sets, for users and groups ([#4773](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4773)), and answers a filter it does not read with 400 `invalidFilter` instead of an empty list, which made an identity provider create the member or team again ([#4772](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4772)).
- Languages: German addresses the reader as *du* and French as *tu* throughout ([#4430](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4430)), and the German app and website now say **Agenten** and **Richtlinien** in the titles and text the v0.5.77 notes listed as unfinished ([#4483](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4483)). Connector setting options ([#4743](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4743)), the fields of a changed automation test ([#4829](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4829)) and the Guardrails overview cards ([#4891](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4891)) read in the reader's language instead of as stored keys and values. The **Language** menu marks the language the page shows, and one that fails to load says so with **Try again** ([#4421](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4421)). The German and French guides use the app's own names for automations, workspaces, connectors, Knowledge and the roles ([#4513](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4513), [#4488](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4488)), and their first-automation tutorial names a run's output section as the app does, **Zurückgegeben** and **Renvoyé** ([#4824](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4824)). German and French app messages that named workspaces, the Owner role and legal hold otherwise now use the labels the app shows ([#4484](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4484)), and labels whose translations load late no longer stay in English ([#4433](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4433)).
- Under any organization accent, in light and dark themes, the Knowledge upload progress bar, a switch's keyboard focus ring and a menu switch's knob are legible ([#2788](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/2788)). The agent equipment menu shows the **Writes data** caption of platform tool grants again ([#3658](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/3658)).
- The website: the contact and demo request forms accept a 2,000-character message in any script, where one in Russian or Japanese was refused with "Something went wrong. Try again." ([#4677](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4677)), and the pricing page writes amounts and counts in the page's language, where the English and French pages showed `1.000+` with region DE ([#4678](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4678)).
- The documentation: a German or French address guessed by translating its path lands on the page it means instead of a 404 or another section's page ([#5037](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5037)); a 404's suggestions carry page titles in the reader's language, section pages have **Previous** and **Next**, and a copy button says when copying failed ([#4909](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4909)); and the [environment reference](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/environment-reference) states the `TOTP_CLIENT_NAME` and `TOTP_ENVIRONMENT` rules whose violation stops the backend at start, such as a name that opens with a symbol or an empty `TOTP_CLIENT_NAME=` line ([#4427](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4427)).
- The CLI: `tale deploy --host` serves its host for that run only and leaves `.env` unchanged, and `tale deploy --dry-run` and `tale reset --dry-run` write nothing ([#4839](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4839)). `tale deploy --override-all` asks for consent before it changes anything, where a decline used to come after the new version was live, and a `--yes` before `deploy` is honoured as one after it ([#5175](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5175)). `tale deploy --dry-run` previews an upgrade on automation writer protocol 2 before the new image is pulled ([#5170](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5170)). `tale restore --stop` also stops restarting and paused containers ([#4980](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4980)). A project whose ID starts with a digit, as `tale init` names one in a folder such as `2024-site`, deploys and rolls back ([#5169](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5169)). A schedule window that names all seven weekdays passes `tale config validate`, `plan` and `apply` ([#4781](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4781)). The Windows installer keeps your PowerShell session open when it fails ([#5174](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5174)). See the [command reference](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/cli-install#command-reference).
- Sandboxes: an agent's processes can no longer read runnerd's token from `/proc`. The token is in no environment of the session, and runnerd makes itself non-dumpable before it starts anything ([#4725](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4725)). CPU pressure counts only as far as the host's CPUs are busy, so one or two sessions building at their own CPU quota no longer hold every new start and refuse every heavy-phase lease on a mostly idle host ([#5146](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5146)). `tale deploy` sizes the [sandbox model gateway's memory](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/environment-reference#sandbox-agent-turns) from the session capacity; its fixed 512 MiB limit had it killed for lack of memory at about 80 sessions ([#5074](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5074)). On Kubernetes, a runner the out-of-memory killer ended reports `SESSION_OOM` instead of a lost session ([#4724](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4724)). An exec whose command has exited is no longer ended as stalled ([#4722](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4722)), and a host that slept no longer counts its sleep against a running exec ([#4721](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4721)). A session whose memory is taken up by what idles in it accepts a command while none runs, instead of refusing every start until the run's deadline ([#4718](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4718)), and destroying a sandbox no longer also destroys a new session opened under the same id meanwhile ([#4106](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4106)).
- The backend: a process that starts while the knowledge database restarts waits up to a minute for it, then verifies the default corpus's search indexes instead of skipping that check until its next restart ([#4035](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4035)). A connection lost during a cursor read no longer crashes the process ([#4066](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4066)). A knowledge database outage is named apart from the platform database's, and a database restart during an MCP call answers a wait instead of an internal error (see the Upgrade notes).

## Upgrade notes

- From v0.5.94 to v0.5.95 the backend applies two migrations at start, and each is safe while the previous image still serves:
  - `0220_short_task_ranks.ts`, a data migration ([#4713](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4713)): every board holding a task rank longer than 64 characters gets short ranks for all of its tasks (every column, archived tasks and subtasks), in the order the board shows them. It locks each such board's task rows before it reads their order, writes 5,000 rows at a time and leaves `updated_at_ms` alone. Boards whose ranks are all at most 64 characters are not touched, and a second run finds nothing to do.
  - `0224_agent_run_host_refused_workers.sql` adds `host_refused_session_ids` to `app.project_agent_runs`, empty by default. A run records there the workers whose sandbox host refused it; the previous image neither writes nor reads the column ([#5006](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5006)).
- The API contract moves from `3.49.0` to `3.51.0`:
  - `3.50.0` ([#4771](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4771)): while the platform database restarts or cannot be reached, an MCP tool call answers a tool result with `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` and `data.retryAfterMs` (5000), and a settings write answers it beside what landed. A resource read, the resource list and a prompt answer JSON-RPC `-32603` with `data.code` and `data.retryAfterMs`. They answered `INTERNAL_ERROR` before, and the call now counts as a refusal, not a failure.
  - `3.51.0` ([#4037](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4037)): `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` now means the platform's own database only. A restart or outage of a knowledge database, the deployment's or an organization's own, answers `KNOWLEDGE_DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE`: the app and REST API answer 503 with that code, `Retry-After: 5` and the request id, where they answered `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE`; MCP `get_knowledge` answers that code with `data.retryAfterMs` (5000), where it answered `status: "unavailable"` with `KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE`. Refused credentials, a missing database and a statement on a connection pool the platform ended itself stay 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`. A client that waits on `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` or reads `KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE` should treat `KNOWLEDGE_DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` the same way.
- The sandbox model gateway's memory limit is no longer a fixed 512 MiB with `tale deploy`: unless the new optional `SANDBOX_LLM_GATEWAY_MEMORY` sets it, the deploy gives the gateway 256 MiB plus 12 MiB for each session of `SANDBOX_MAX_SESSIONS`, at least `512m` (`3328m` with the capacity unset). The shipped compose files use `3328m`; with them and a capacity above 256 sessions, set `SANDBOX_LLM_GATEWAY_MEMORY`. On Kubernetes nothing changes by itself: raise `resources.limits.memory` of the gateway's Deployment for a larger capacity. The limit is a ceiling, not memory reserved at start ([#5074](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5074)).
- The sandbox runtime's runnerd now receives its token on a descriptor, marks itself non-dumpable, and stops if either fails; its start log line `token=descriptor; dumpable=false` says both held ([#4725](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4725)).
- `tale deploy --host <domain>` no longer writes `HOST`, `SITE_URL` or `TLS_MODE=letsencrypt` into `.env`: the host serves that one run, and a running proxy the deploy does not recreate (no `--stop`) keeps the host it was started with, which the deploy names. If you used `--host` to change the deployment's host for good, set `HOST` and `SITE_URL` (and `TLS_MODE` if it should change) in `.env` ([#4839](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4839)).
- `tale deploy --override-all` without a terminal now needs `--yes`, and refuses before it changes anything (exit 4, "Nothing was changed.") where it used to fail after the new version was live. Add `--yes` to a script that runs it ([#5175](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5175)).
- `tale restore` without `--stop` now refuses while a project container is restarting or paused, not only while one runs, and names them; see [restore the matching data and version](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/operate/backups-and-restore#restore-the-matching-data-and-version) ([#4980](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4980)).
- Single sign-on claim rules and mappings that name a claim containing dots start to match at each member's next sign-in, and can give members the roles and teams they name. Review such rules before you upgrade. A SCIM client that filtered users on anything but `userName eq` or groups on anything but `displayName eq` now gets 400 `invalidFilter`: set your identity provider to match on those attributes ([#4775](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4775), [#4772](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4772)).
- Direct chat with a custom OpenAI-format provider or a gateway that lists its own models now calls that gateway's Responses API for OpenAI models whose tools are served only there. A gateway that refuses it before streaming (400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 415, 422 or 501) is asked on Chat Completions in the same round, and for 15 minutes after; nothing needs configuring.
- From this release on, a Release run moves the `:latest` images and GitHub's **Latest** release only for a stable version at least as high as every published one, so re-running an older release no longer moves them back. A run uses the release workflow of its tag's commit, so a re-run of a tag cut before this release still moves them ([#4740](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4740)).
